title: My Dragon Ate My Homework
description: Prove to your teacher that the dragon really did it
template:
Everyone knows "my dog ate my homework" is the oldest excuse in the book. But when I told Mrs. Pickleton that my DRAGON ate my homework, she said, "{name}, I'd like to see that."

So after school, I brought her home to meet {dragon}.

{dragon} is a {color} dragon with {adj1} wings and breath that smells like old {food}. When we walked in, {dragon} was lying on the couch watching cartoons and burping little puffs of smoke. Every burp went {noise}!

"This is the dragon who ate my {subject} homework," I told Mrs. Pickleton.

{dragon} looked up and said, "In my defense, it looked {adj2}."

Mrs. Pickleton did not believe it. So {dragon} sneezed, and out flew {number} pieces of paper, all covered in slobber. And there it was, my homework, a little burnt around the edges.

"Well," said Mrs. Pickleton, "I suppose I believe you now."

Then {dragon} got a gleam in its eye. "Since you're here, how about a ride?" Before she could answer, we were all on its back, soaring over {place}. Mrs. Pickleton screamed, then laughed, then started to {verb} with her arms in the air.

When we landed, she was covered in {pluralnoun} and grinning from ear to ear.

"You get an A on your homework," she said. "And {dragon} gets a gold star for flying."

I never had to use the dog excuse again.
